DiskRescue 0.2.2 adds Linux on Arm64: get photos and videos back from failing, formatted or "needs formatting" SD cards, USB drives and disks on Arm computers, and repair the files that came back broken.

## Linux on Arm64

- **New in 0.2.2:** `diskrescue-v0.2.2-aarch64-linux.tar.gz` (static `diskrescue` and `diskrescue-tui`, plus the desktop app) and `diskrescue_0.2.2_arm64.deb`. They are built natively on Arm in CI, not cross-compiled, and the same checks run on both architectures: the full test suite, every binary is checked to be the right CPU, the installed package starts all three programs, and the desktop app opens a window.
- The x86-64 downloads are unchanged: `diskrescue-v0.2.2-x86_64-linux.tar.gz` and `diskrescue_0.2.2_amd64.deb`.
- Install the package with `sudo apt install ./diskrescue_0.2.2_amd64.deb` (or `_arm64.deb`) on Ubuntu 24.04 or newer, or unpack the tarball; the programs in it need no installation.

## Downloads

| | x86-64 | Arm64 (aarch64) |
|---|---|---|
| Debian / Ubuntu package (24.04 and newer) | `diskrescue_0.2.2_amd64.deb` | `diskrescue_0.2.2_arm64.deb` |
| Linux tarball | `diskrescue-v0.2.2-x86_64-linux.tar.gz` | `diskrescue-v0.2.2-aarch64-linux.tar.gz` |
| Windows zip (unsigned) | `diskrescue-v0.2.2-x86_64-windows.zip` | `diskrescue-v0.2.2-aarch64-windows.zip` |

`SHA256SUMS` lists every download.

## Windows

Nothing changes in the programs since 0.2.1: native x86-64 and ARM64 builds, as a zip here and as a Microsoft Store package (https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/9NS2VVPWDM9T). The zips are not signed, so SmartScreen or Smart App Control may warn about them or block them. They need no Visual C++ Redistributable. Reading a whole drive needs administrator rights; the desktop app offers **Restart as administrator**.

## Known limits

- Tested on synthetic disk images, simulated failing devices, generated media and Windows virtual disks; not yet on a wide range of real failing hardware or real camera RAW files.
- Deleted files on SSDs are usually erased by TRIM and rarely recoverable.
- Not yet supported: fragmented-file carving, APFS, HFS+, btrfs, XFS, encrypted volumes.
